report:
Reviewed the full subtyping_and_coercion claim, all six ordinary implementation entries, three ordinary annotated tests and one TODO test. Requirements: subtype success preserves representation and adds no conversion; coercion occurs at a coercion site, can change representation, and is explicit in completed Typed IR; never-to-any is coercion only. This assessment is limited to the core relation/coercion paths and associated tests. It does not evaluate the separately authored unary-dereference behavior in expr.rs; no selected test or relation-path dependency required that behavior.

Implementation: InferCtx::require_sub first canonicalizes operands, accepts equal roots, recursively relates shared-reference referents, uses equality for mutable-reference referents, and otherwise requires equality. There is no never-to-any arm. unify_in_probe compares skeleton and child arity before recursively unifying children, so Never differs from integer/other constructors and cannot be smuggled beneath invariant references. skeleton.rs preserves constructor identity, reference mutability, array constants, tuple/function arity and nominal/alias identities. The currently represented subtype rules therefore preserve structural representation rather than inserting a runtime conversion; this is not a claim of a complete Rust variance or layout-analysis engine.

InferCtx::coerce_expr checks top-level source Never with a non-Never target, otherwise invokes require_sub. At a never coercion it allocates TyExprData::NeverToAny with the target type while retaining the operand and its source type. For a block tail it recurses to the tail and creates a correctly typed block. Expected-expression checking in expr.rs invokes the coercion helper after synthesis; function body completion in fns.rs invokes it against the declared return type and retains contextual diagnostics on failure. Unknown targets are deferred rather than immediately unified to Never, allowing later arguments to constrain them; default_deferred_never_targets chooses Never only for still-unconstrained targets. finalize.rs copies NeverToAny into the completed tree, removing the wrapper when the finalized target itself is Never. Non-coercing subtype success returns the original expression. These inspected paths distinguish representation-preserving relation from explicit conversion.

Test adequacy: never_to_any_is_not_subtyping_beneath_mutable_references supplies source &mut ! -> &mut u32 and expects the concrete Sage mismatch. Its rustc-only marker accounts for the separate feature gate on never parameter syntax while the shared marker requires the return mismatch; that qualification is visible in the body. top_level_never_coercion_preserves_source_and_result_types expects both a loop typed ! and a separate coercion typed u32 for a u32-returning function, while the !-returning function has only the original never loop. generic_never_coercions_follow_other_arguments_in_either_order expects pair(loop {}, true) and pair(true, loop {}) both to instantiate bool parameters and expose explicit bool coercion nodes, while single(loop {}) resolves to fn(!) without a redundant conversion. These assertions distinguish source and result types and guard premature fallback/order sensitivity.

Captured compile-test helpers show real isolated source projects, production Sage body queries, diagnostic matching and exact expectation comparisons; the observer emits coercion rows only for completed TyExprData::NeverToAny nodes and retains the original operand row. FrozenType renders actual checked types, not expected answers. Captured rustc execution/output validation confirms independent compiler diagnostic checks; no rustc or test invocation was made in this review. Source observation/correlation dependencies were also captured. The snapshots are substantive assertions, not just annotation or test-name evidence.

The associated TODO inference_subtyping_and_coercion retains the full rule matrix and layout evidence. Its never/invariant/core scenarios now have partial ordinary coverage, but it still calls for focused relation tests covering every implemented subtype/coercion rule and demonstrating layout preservation. It contains no assertions and is not counted as completed verification. Completing that remaining matrix requires representative source-level constructors and relation-level cases, including nested/shared-reference rules and failure paths, with explicit typed-tree observations at conversion sites. No claim is made that all Rust coercions or a general layout engine already exist. No new suspected defect was identified in the reviewed core paths.

Commands executed: fresh review start with coordinator instructions, source and all associated-test inspection, review read captures of inference design and compile harness/observer/source/type/rustc helpers. No tests or build executed, no source edits. Central suite results are separate evidence. No requested edits; broad relation/layout verification remains explicitly deferred.
